facts.statement: The study used a randomized, sham-controlled crossover design with ten human participants who had no motor, neurological, or psychiatric disorders.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants performed a P300 speller task before and after stimulation while an attention-demanding task was active during the stimulation period.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers measured P300 peak amplitudes, the ability to distinguish targets from non-targets, and offline classification accuracy across different brain channels.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Real stimulation led to a statistically significant improvement in offline discrimination accuracy specifically at the P4 brain channel compared to sham stimulation.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Despite better offline discrimination, the stimulation did not result in improved real-time character selection performance by the participants.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants with lower initial performance showed larger improvements, though these gains were not statistically significant, suggesting tDCS might help this specific group more.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors conclude that while the method is feasible for modulating brain activity, more research is needed to understand how these local changes affect the full decoding process.
facts.subject: humans
